$2048 FOR FARCASTER CLIENTS

Anyone can build a Farcaster client and run a read node to get data from the protocol. There are developer tutorials on the web[1,2,3,4], but your mission in this prize, should you choose to accept it, is to improve them by collecting all relevant info and making it incredibly easy. 

Specifically, we want you to get it down to three commands, as described in your quickstart and then detailed in your tutorial:

(0) Provision necessary compute via script (1) Set up a Snapchain read node (2) Create a client that reads from that node

The read node should run on its own, with no API keys from anyone. You just furnish the compute. Note that a read node syncs the network but does not accept writes, so your client should read from your own node and submit casts to a validator endpoint; the tutorial should explain how that works.

The client should be able to import an existing seed phrase for an account that already has storage, use that seed phrase to issue the client its own app key (one small Optimism transaction), and then post with that key: read the feed, post casts, follow and react, and include/exclude casts from any other client.

In addition to the quickstart at the top of the page, the tutorial should be mobile- and desktop-friendly, and should explain key protocol concepts as it goes (e.g. FIDs, custody addresses, app keys, Snapchain messages, read nodes vs validators, storage rent). Anything that someone running a client and read node would need to know.

You can use AI, but your output must *not* be AI slop, as ultimately determined in our sole discretion. To qualify for a prize, you need to have at least one other human user successfully go through your tutorial and create a read node and client. They then need to post on Farcaster publicly vouching for the quality of your work.

You can go the extra mile of course, like adding Chinese translation, adding a 59s vertical video, and so on. But getting more humans to vouch for your tutorial will be the most powerful signal.

To enter, submit a reply to this post with three URLs: (1) your microsite with the quickstart + tutorial, (2) the associated GitHub repository with all MIT-licensed open source code, and (3) the link to your voucher's public endorsement on Farcaster.

Prize: $2,048 first place, $512 second place, $128 each for honorable mentions, subject to whether there are enough good submissions. Paid in USDC to your public Farcaster wallet address by default.

Deadline: your reply with three URLs must be submitted within seven days exactly from this post's timestamp.

That’s it! Go learn the Farcaster protocol yourself, help others learn how to boot up their own clients, earn crypto for doing it, and increase practical freedom of association.

Hello everyone! Network School is acquiring Farcaster.

Our goal is to turn this client into a family-friendly place where you can learn technology, earn cryptocurrency, have fun with the community, achieve your milestones in life, and gradually build a high-trust offline society. Anyone of any race, religion, class, or nationality is welcome so long as they cooperate with other members and share broadly techno-optimist values (a16z.com/the-techno-optimist-manifesto/).

To get there, we’ll need a new moderation policy. Rather than the Soviet Union of digital tyranny which typified the 2010s, or the Somalia of lawless digital anarchy that characterizes today’s online environment, we seek to intentionally build the first Singapore of social media. We get there in four steps: institute law-and-order, create a decentralized democracy, publish a written social smart contract, and then hold an ongoing series of meetups with our newly invigorated community.

(1) Step one is law and order. In the pre-Internet world, it was simply unheard of to run up to a stranger and start cursing at them. We’re restoring that offline norm online. Much like how President Bukele jailed a small fraction of repeat offenders to essentially eliminate crime (https://tinyurl.com/39hwed77) in El Salvador, we’ve moderated out the small fraction of repeat offenders that have been muted or blocked by many accounts to stop random attacks within this Farcaster reference client.

We’ve done this by using both humans and AI to crunch millions of posts. Of course, there will always be some false positives, and we do have an appeals process in the event you either (a) believe your account was unfairly moderated or (b) believe you were fairly moderated, but want to commit to changing your behavior in the future. From one vantage point, other social media platforms have had a moderation-and-appeal process for a long time, so in one sense we’re really just catching up on technical debt and getting to industry standard. However, in another sense, unlike pre-existing tech platforms, we’re actually being very concrete about the techno-optimist values we stand for — and giving you a concrete democratic choice over your digital governance, which leads us to step two.

(2) Step two is decentralized digital democracy. As described at farcaster.xyz/~/vote, you can vote with your crypto wallet, your onchain ballot, and eventually your feet (via a Farcon/NS meetup) for our social Singapore. Many of you have already done so, like @linda, @mazmhussain, and @phil. In fact, as of the time of this writing, we’re at 92.9% support for Network School Farcaster, and you can see the onchain votes provably streaming in here: basescan.org/token/0x4ecfed276c566aeb49da1f3a888e8dbb7263028d

Of course, you can also vote for another client, or build your own. After all, the Farcaster client has been open sourced (github.com/farcasterxyz/client), and the Farcaster protocol is already open. So with today’s AI tooling you can rapidly boot up whatever client you want.

The only limitation is the same one the Ethereum Foundation implements: you can’t use Farcaster, Warpcast, Neynar, Network State, or Network School-related names to launch any coin, token, or commercial project. You can use the Farcaster protocol under the hood, just like Google uses Linux under the hood, but you can’t call your app or digital asset Farcaster itself. The goal is to prevent user confusion and crypto scams.

(3) Step three towards building the first Singapore of social media is to publish examples of good and bad behavior, what an earlier generation might call “Goofus and Gallant.” We have a v1 of the social smart contract and the corresponding "Network Code" up at farcaster.xyz/~/contract. We’ll update it over time with specific AI prompts, concrete examples of pro-social behavior that we want in the app (like posting technical tutorials, hosting offline events, and the like) and also examples of anti-social behavior that we don’t want.

(4) Finally, step four is to begin hosting online and offline meetups with the community of members that have opted into the new vision. We may do a meetup like Farcon (https://farcon.xyz), an in-person event at Network School in Astana, or an online event like our previous 1729 VR meetups (https://x.com/mckaywrigley/status/1466287496589840392), or all of the above. In each case, admission will be at least partially token-gated to those who voted for the new social smart contract. This way we start from a baseline of common values, techno-optimist goals, and provable democratic legitimacy. From that solid foundation, we can build a true digital community. And together we can cooperate at a scale no social network has ever seen before.

So, that's the idea. We’re looking forward to building the first Singapore of social media with you. If you want to join us, please make your choice at farcaster.xyz/~/vote.

Individually alpha is collectively beta.

That’s actually the centrist argument against the sort of caricatured ultra-masculinity that’s in vogue today. I understand how that ideology arose, but it actually makes you weak, because it inhibits scaled cooperation.

Essentially: in almost every context in life you can’t and shouldn’t be the leader. Even Elon isn’t running the water supply or sewing his own clothes. In those contexts, he’s just an individual like any other, operating in a context where he isn’t the boss. A “beta” if you absolutely must, or better yet a peer — even if he’s a superalpha at SpaceX.

Steve Jobs understood this too. Also a superalpha at Apple, he nevertheless understood in an email towards the end of his life (attached below) how dependent he was on the rest of humanity in most other contexts.

What few understand is that being a leader is actually a huge responsibility. You simply can’t be at the top of every hierarchy in the world nor should you seek to be. A good life is more about win/win cooperation than the quixotic pursuit of zero-sum dominance. The fact that Western societies have lost faith in both God and the State is part of what’s driven them towards the most primitive sort of chest-thumping Internet he-manism, but being “alpha” all the time doesn’t scale.

Cooperation does.

Thesis

Farcaster should unapologetically use AI to keep the vibe positive and pro-builder in the default client.

Anyone can do what they want in other clients, but defaults matter.
(I know Facebook et al has been doing this for a while. But it’d be different on an open platform such as Farcaster. Opt-in algorithmic moderation, like AI moderated subreddits.)

AI could determine whether a Farcaster post is on topic. And whether it’s more positive or negative than you intended. In general, it can scale up opt-in content moderation.

Many kinds of UX uses that are just beginning to be explored.

AI is for prototyping, not production.

(At least, not without heavy review.)

In short: tech can see the bad of AI, but we can also see the good. 

But many (most?) will only see the bad. Not just of AI, but of all tech. And the Western left is already against capitalists, and the Western right is already against immigrants. The Western center will soon turn against the phones (arguably they already have). And in any relative (let alone absolute) economic downturn, the West as a whole may associate AI, crypto, the Internet, and tech itself with Western decline.

Even if the rest of the world is actually rising with the Internet, and many Westerners rising with it.

Even if the bugs in the Information Revolution get worked out over time, as they did with the Industrial Revolution.

Even if Jonathan Haidt’s (reasonable) arguments against the use of phones mean that we actually need a consensually moderated Internet, rather than no Internet.

Even if continued technological progress is (obviously) the only way to create wealth.

And even if Unabomber-style Luddism will actually leave people who’re angry about decline even poorer than they were before.

It doesn’t matter. A number of trends will fuse to make the Western middle class angrily scapegoat tech as a class. The wealth of tech, the foreignness of it, the downsides of AI and crypto and social, the nostalgia for the pre-Internet world.

Tech will be attacked as a class, much as the capitalist class was attacked in the 1900s. But history is running in reverse, and while the conflict will be similar this time there will be a different outcome.

In the 20th century, the capitalists who built the modern world essentially lost. In Russia and China and places like that they were just murdered. Whereas in America, men like Carnegie and Rockefeller and Mellon were expropriated by the state. The middle of the 20th century was the zenith of centralized government and the nadir of entrepreneurship.

But now history is running in reverse. The techno capitalist isn’t tied to the land as much as the industrial capitalist was.

That means we can exit, remain agile, and build Internet First societies. We can build models for what societies built on the Internet rather than disrupted by it would look like. But we are going to have to do this. We are going to need to build legitimacy too, by putting democracy onchain like we did for capitalism. We are ultimately going to have to remake every institution, and indeed the world, on an Internet-First basis.

AI is amazing. But AI is also awful.

I see so much sloppy, low quality, absolutely midwit work done with AI.

The worst part is that many AI users have no taste whatsoever, and are actually proud of their completely error-prone midwit slop. And they don’t understand that the numbers AI generates are often wrong, because they themselves aren’t good with numbers. Even worse is when they deny they used AI to generate the slop.

AI has essentially created a completely new class of midwit, separate and distinct and only partially overlapping with the US university educated midwit. It’s similar in that both are just mindlessly regurgitating what they learned. But I can’t believe that I actually prefer, at least some of the time, the style of the old midwit.

Bring NPC back?! AI is the new NPC.

To be clear, I see all the positive sides of AI. It’s amazing for data analysis, for visualizing via Midjourney, for organizing search results, for summarizing large documents, and for cleaning up audio transcripts. It’s often a better doctor than a doctor, or a better lawyer than a lawyer.

But only in skilled hands. High IQ prompting and verifying gets high IQ output. Low IQ prompting and verifying gets complete slop. I think of AI as amplified intelligence, as opposed to artificial intelligence.

Moreover, the text that AI generates is placeholder text. It’s the new lorem ipsum, it’s lorem aipsum. It is at best a suggestion and meant to be completely rewritten in your voice. By contrast, AI images and video are higher quality, in part because they are more obviously AI.

Meanwhile, the Chinese are focusing much more on AI in the physical world, for drones, robotics, self-driving, and manufacturing. Elon is doing this but relatively few others are. Those physical use cases, at least right now, are pulling out of their trough-of-sorrow stage and getting to full production. Self-driving cars are real and they are here.

Anyway, the problems with digital AI may be solvable. We’ll have all kinds of tools to detect AI and prove that something is not AI. And it’s very possible that models could evolve to generate higher quality results, or at least highly personalized results, so that it’s not the same generic slop from so many.

But just saying: I love AI, but I also kind of hate when it’s used badly. And I can see why others will just see the downsides and not the upsides. It’s extremely similar to crypto in this way. And it’s very simple for people to just say “no AI, no crypto” without parsing through the downsides to see the upsides.

I do think we will get through the other side and turn AI into a power tool with a higher hit rate. Just like we don’t think that much about people getting electrocuted by power lines. The bugs will get worked out. But it’ll be both cultural and technological adaptation.

The Internet is going to win.

It will win much bigger than most people yet realize.

And few if any institutions that predated the Internet will survive the Internet.

So we’ll need to rebuild Internet-first replacements for those institutions.

Does “generational wealth” even exist? And should it? I am not so sure.

(1) First, if you have 2 children and 4 grandchildren and 8 great grandchildren and so on (let alone more!), then your fortune is divided by 2^n, and so are your genes. So your bloodline isn’t set forever. Indeed, unless there’s extreme levels of consanguinity, it’s diluted quite quickly.

(2) Second, very few tactics for wealth compounding get you a reliable 2X every 25 years. What happens instead is that in most jurisdictions (save the UK), you have some titanic war, inflation, or the like every several decades. That zeros out the ledger, interrupts compounding, and has everyone start from scratch.

(3) Third, many children (and especially grandchildren) who inherit wealth tend to fritter it away. The documentary Born Rich shows how the J&J heir essentially became a socialist (for others of course) because he felt so much guilt over his unearned wealth. There is a saying: shirtsleeves to shirtsleeves in three generations. It’s much easier to spend a fortune than to make one.

(4) Fourth, and relatedly, it’s not obvious that great fortune is even that huge an asset in the modern era. China and India came up from nothing in one lifetime. Startups do this even more quickly. I’m not saying capital has *no* use, but it’s much less of a moat in the Information Age than many think.

(5) Next, outside the West, we are in the age of hyperdeflation. China is making everything in the physical world extraordinarily cheap, while the Internet has made everything digital extremely inexpensive. This is the opposite of what American Anarchy represents, with cars set on fire and money printed, but China and the Internet are crashing prices for everything.

(6) Next, many of these new huge fortunes in the West are a function of the debasement of the dollar rather than genuine wealth creation. $100M just isn’t what it was even 10 years ago, perhaps not even 5 years ago.

(7) Finally, generational wealth is a vision of stasis. Secure the bag and chill out. But that’s just not what humanity is about. It’s about constant, relentless, technological progress over generations. A big pile of cash by itself won’t  get us eternal life, won’t get us the infinite frontier. If you want to see the stars, and touch Mars — only technology will do that.

Hence: generational progress over generational wealth. The former is about production, the latter is about consumption.
